do.name: Climb the ruined city to the Frankish castle
do.detail: Stone lanes and stairs gain about 250 metres from the lower gate to the keep, where the whole Evrotas plain opens up below.

do.name: Stand inside the Palace of the Despots
do.detail: The only Byzantine royal palace still standing anywhere, reopened after a long restoration of its great vaulted hall.

do.name: Visit Pantanassa, the convent still in use
do.detail: Nuns keep the terraces and the shaded courtyard, and the late Palaiologan frescoes inside are the best preserved on the hill.

do.name: See the wall paintings at Peribleptos
do.detail: A monastery church built partly into the rock face, its fourteenth century cycle counted among the finest Byzantine painting in Greece.

do.name: The cathedral courtyard and its museum
do.detail: Carved slabs, coins and church silver are displayed beside the Metropolis, where an imperial coronation is said to have taken place.

do.name: Detour to Agia Sofia in the upper town
do.detail: The court church sits on a terrace beside the palace, a quiet stop with a drop straight down the hillside from its edge.
